landing.heroLead: Your land, on the map and in the register.
landing.whatBody: One public register for every plot in Mogadishu: surveyed on the map, checked by the land office, published for objections, then registered with a unique number you can rely on.

register.title: Register your land
register.body: Apply online or at the district office. A surveyor draws your plot and you get a Parcel Unique Number (PUN).

pay.title: Pay property tax
pay.body: See your bill and pay by EVC Plus, Zaad, Sahal, eDahab, bank or cash, with a receipt every time.

verify.title: Check before you buy
verify.body: Every registered plot is on public notice first, and every certificate carries a QR code anyone can verify.

owner.label: Property owners
owner.text: Your plot gets a boundary, a number and a record of its owners — so nobody can quietly sell what is yours.

buyer.label: Buyers
buyer.text: Before you pay, look the plot up, check who owns it and whether anyone has objected or a dispute is open.

bank.label: Banks
bank.text: A verified title with a known boundary is something you can lend against. Liens and transfers are recorded on the same register.

staff.label: District staff
staff.text: Applications, surveys, verification and registration in one workspace, with every decision recorded and checked by a second person.

landing.howBody: Seven steps, each recorded. You can follow your application at any time with its number.

apply.title: Apply
apply.body: Owners, documents and a pin on the map — online, at the office or with a field officer.

fee.title: Application fee
fee.body: Paid by mobile money or at the cashier, or waived by finance with a recorded reason.

survey.title: Survey
survey.body: A surveyor measures the plot on site and draws its boundary; overlaps with neighbours are caught here.

verify.title: Verification
verify.body: A land officer checks documents, identities and the survey.

notice.title: Public notice
notice.body: The plot is published so anyone with a claim can object before it is registered.

register.title: Registration
register.body: The registrar approves and the plot gets its PUN and account number.

certificate.title: Certificate
certificate.body: Collect your title certificate and property ID card, each with a QR check.

valuation.title: Valuation
valuation.subtitle: Prices for land and houses: by neighbourhood and house type, fees, transfer types, and the requests to decide.
valuation.noAssessmentsBody: Assess a registered parcel from its page, or a whole neighbourhood at once.
valuation.assessNeighbourhoodBody: Every registered parcel in the neighbourhood gets this year's assessment. Parcels with an open appeal are skipped.
valuation.assessedCount: {assessed, plural, one {# parcel} other {# parcels}} assessed, {skipped} skipped.

valuation.noRatesBody: Without a neighbourhood rate the default rate from settings is used.

valuation.deleteExemptionBody: The pending request is removed. It can be asked for again later.
valuation.deleteAppealBody: The open appeal is removed and the assessment stands as issued.

valuation.deleteRateBody: Only a rate no assessment was made with can be deleted. For a rate already used, add a new rate from a later date instead.

valuation.stampDutyHint: Charged on a bill when the transfer is sent for approval. 0 = none.

valuation.buildingFlatsNote: Flats: ground floor Apartment, upper floors Upper Floors

billing.runsSubtitle: The system bills each property by itself on its own anniversary: every day it finds the properties whose year is up, ends their certificate and makes that year's tax bill. When the bill is paid, a new certificate comes by itself. Use New billing run as a backup.
billing.newRunBody: Choose the year, the fee and the districts. A preview with counts, totals and exceptions follows before anything is billed.
billing.feeTypeHint: Property tax uses each parcel's assessment for the year; other fees use their fixed amount.
billing.noRunsBody: Bills are made by themselves on each property's anniversary. Runs made that way show here too.

steps.refreshBody: Recount parcels, totals and exceptions with today's data.
steps.submitBody: Finance reviews the preview and approves it. You can't change it after submitting; cancel and start again instead.
steps.approveBody: The run is approved as previewed. Then press Generate invoices to create the bills and text the owners.
steps.generateBody: One invoice is created per parcel and the owners are sent an SMS. Parcels already invoiced for this period are skipped, so this is safe to retry.
steps.cancelBody: No invoices are created. Give the reason; it is recorded.
steps.issueNowBody: One bill is made for each land in the preview straight away, without waiting for approval, and the owners are sent an SMS.

notes.revenue: Money received, by the month it was received, split by what it paid for. Unallocated credit is money not yet matched to a bill.
notes.arrears: Open balances today, by how long they are past the due date. Dates don't apply.
notes.collection: Bills issued in the period and how much of them has been paid or credited.
notes.registrations: Applications submitted and parcels registered per month. Median days runs from submission to registration.
notes.cashiers: Shifts opened in the period, what each cashier took, and cash differences at close.
notes.income: From the ledger. Income is what was billed and earned; money in is what reached cash, mobile money, card or bank; money out is refunds and reversals.
notes.billing: Bills issued in the period by month, district and fee type, with what has been paid and what is still owed.
notes.invoices: Every bill issued in the period. Paid includes credits.
notes.payments: Every payment received in the period, with the bills it paid, the cashier and the point of sale.
notes.certificates: Certificates and ID cards issued in the period.
notes.parcels: Parcels as they are today. Partial means land not yet registered (draft, surveyed or verified, often with a provisional shape).
notes.owners: Current owners, co-owners and heirs, one row per owner and parcel. Dates don't apply.
notes.locations: Districts, sections, sectors and neighbourhoods with the parcels in each and whether a boundary is drawn. Dates don't apply.
notes.paymentTypes: For each revenue category (fee type), how much came in by Cash, EVC Plus, eDahab, ZAAD, Bank transfer, Visa / Mastercard and Other, with the grand total. Click a category or an amount to see those payments.
notes.collections: Total collections = Cash + EVC Plus + eDahab + ZAAD + Bank transfer (+ Visa / Mastercard and Other), per day, per week (Monday to Sunday) or per month. By default only payments a finance officer verified count.
notes.collectionsCashier: What each cashier collected by way of paying, how much is not yet verified, how many of their days are reconciled, and the shortages and excess found.
notes.shortages: Each cashier day reconciled in the period: recorded against actually received, the difference per way of paying (± column), shortage = recorded − received, excess = received − recorded, and who prepared and approved it.
notes.unreconciled: Payments not yet in an approved cashier reconciliation: pending, verified or disputed, oldest first.
notes.transfers: Transfers started or decided in the period, with the owners before and after and any transfer duty still owed.
notes.permits: Building permits asked for or decided in the period.
notes.disputes: Disputes opened in the period, and every one still open however old.
notes.demolished: Houses taken down in the period (by the demolition date), and whether they were rebuilt or brought back.
notes.surveyZones: Survey zones as they are today: houses recorded against the target, and owners added but still waiting for their land.
notes.certificateStatus: Every registered house and its latest certificate. Houses with no valid certificate this year are listed first, with what they still owe.
notes.staffActivity: What each staff member did in the period. Changes counts every save they made in the system.
notes.messages: Messages the system made in the period, by kind: sent, still waiting, failed or stopped.

help.prepare: The old database comes from its backup file. The new database is this system's books (Supabase). Nothing from the file is ever run against either.
help.backups: The old file is kept unchanged in private storage and read back to check its fingerprint. The books (accounts, journal, periods) are copied before the run; the real migration can't start without that copy.
help.inspectOld: Every table found in the old file: its rows, columns and types, keys and links, repeated rows and empty values. Pick a table to look inside.
help.inspectNew: The tables a migration writes to here, as they are now. They are never changed in shape or made again. * = must be filled.
help.tables: Say what each old table holds. Names don't decide anything: a table called anything can hold accounts, journal entries or journal lines. Tables not needed are ignored.
help.columns: For each of our fields, choose the old column and how it is changed on the way. The right-hand column shows what the first old rows become; ⚠ means a value can't be read that way.
help.ids: Old IDs are never reused. Each old account is matched to one of ours, or made as a new account with a 4-digit code; each old district value to one of our districts. The ID map keeps old → new for every record.
help.preview: Work out every record from the old rows and the mapping. Each one is ready, or says why it can't go. Do this again after changing the mapping.
help.test: Runs the whole migration and then puts everything back, so the books don't change. Shows exactly what would be created and what would fail.
help.historical: How old records are kept once they are in. Owners, land, bills and payments come in quietly: no SMS, no commissions, nothing posted to this year's books.
help.production: Accounts, then journal entries; then owners, land, bills and payments, then demolished land is marked. Each record is checked as it goes in; one that fails is left out and listed, the rest go in.
help.report: What is in the books now compared with the old data, the trial balance of what was migrated, and every step taken.
